text:
ashley: Heads up — about 25% of eu-west3 GPU nodes went NotReady / tainted NoSchedule after the late-night kernel-image roll. Training queues piling up. device-plugin pods are CrashLooping. Anyone already looking?

chris: I'm pulling node status now. Can you paste `kubectl get nodes | grep gpu-eu3` output?

ashley: Sure:
```
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide | egrep "gpu-eu3"
gpu-eu3-001   NotReady   <none>   4d   v1.26.3   10.128.3.12   ...
gpu-eu3-002   NotReady   <none>   3d   v1.26.3   10.128.3.13
gpu-eu3-003   Ready      <none>   5d   v1.26.3   10.128.3.14
```
and kube-system device plugin logs (short):
```
E0318 03:12:08.123 1 driver.go:241] failed to init driver: module 'nvidia_uvm' not found
E0318 03:12:08.125 1 plugin.go:88] nvidia device plugin exiting: missing kernel symbols
```

maria: This matches the kernel-module mismatch we've seen before — image bump pulled kernel 6.x but drivers are for 5.15/525 series. The DKMS/driver package didn't rebuild the uvm module. Likely caused by the node image rollout yesterday.

oncall_tom: If nodes don't come Ready the autoscaler will keep trying but new pods won't schedule. Short-term mitigation: cordon the bad nodes and route workloads to fallback CPU or to the dedicated GPU reserve. Also set scheduler-sig to prefer non-gpu for low-priority jobs.

chris: Can we restart `nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset` to see if it re-probes after a driver load? If module missing, restart won't help. Need either reinstall driver or roll back node image. Which has lower blast radius?

ashley: Reinstalling driver via apt on each node is heavy. The node image rollback should be faster via cloud nodepool version pin (we can suspend the rollout). Requesting rollback now; opening GCP console.

sre-bot: Incident #INC-4321 created: 'eu-west3 GPU nodes NotReady after kernel-image rollout' — paging @oncall_tom

maria: Also prepping a short script to run on nodes to check `lsmod | grep nvidia` and `sudo dkms status`. If dkms shows 'no such module' we can attempt `sudo apt-get install --reinstall nvidia-driver-535 -y && sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm`.

oncall_tom: Rolling back node pool image to previous stable (image-id: rwd-ubuntu-20240214) now. I'll cordon the failing ones and schedule a drain one at a time after rollback.

ashley: Thanks — jobs are backing up but we've enabled experimental CPU fallback so critical pipelines keep going.

(30m later)

ashley: Update: rollback started, device-plugin restarts after nodes come back. So far 2/3 previously NotReady nodes moved to Ready and pods scheduled.

chris: Good. After rollback we'll run a one-off to reinstall driver and check kernel headers. Also adding a preflight on future image rollouts: check `nvidia-smi` and `dkms status` in canaries before rolling to gpupool.

maria: Filing a postmortem draft and will include checklist: canary gpu-node check, rollback automation, and alerting on device-plugin CrashLoopBackOff.

ashley: Nice work. Reopen if any regressions :thumbsup:
